question.text: Mutual fund scheme performance reporting requires disclosure of:

answer.text: Scheme returns alongside the benchmark index used by the AMC/trustees, for comparison
Only the absolute scheme return, with no benchmark reference
A new self-selected benchmark every month

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook notes that SEBI requires equity fund returns to be published alongside benchmark indices selected by the AMC and trustees, so that investors can compare scheme performance against an appropriate benchmark. The Trap: Random or self-selected monthly benchmarks would defeat the purpose of comparability, and reporting only absolute returns hides whether the scheme beat or lagged its reference index. Note: For PMS, benchmark choice follows APMI-prescribed options; for mutual fund schemes the AMC/trustees select an appropriate index in line with SEBI norms.
